reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) concerns high-entropy alloy coatings on Q235 steel, not the intrinsic microstructure or corrosion behavior of untreated Q235 steel. Neither passage provides any data on grain boundary distribution, inclusions, oxide film uniformity, or the effect of annealing on Q235 steel itself. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited prior evidence.
premises: Microstructural heterogeneity (grain boundaries, inclusions) in Q235 steel causes nonuniform iron oxide films
Nonuniform oxide films create differential electrochemical potentials that initiate localized corrosion
Thermal annealing homogenizes the microstructure of Q235 steel
